title: Data center boom is pushing prices higher, according to Fed officials
source_used: Newser (relays the Washington Post report; cites Reuters for the split on rates)
key_facts: Minutes of the Fed's September meeting, released on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026, show officials now see the AI infrastructure boom, more than tariffs, as a key force keeping goods prices elevated.
Policymakers cited a rush of borrowing to fund data centres, chips and related hardware as 'surging AI-related investments' that could push demand beyond what businesses can supply.
Core goods prices (excluding food and energy) are still rising at a brisk pace even as the effect of past tariff hikes fades.
The Fed now expects inflation to stay above its 2% goal until 2029.
Officials believe AI will eventually boost productivity and output but admit they do not know how big or how fast those gains will be.

The minutes show a split on the reasoning for raising interest rates: 'some participants' backed a rise to counter rising energy prices, while others said demand-driven inflation makes higher rates necessary (per Reuters, via Newser).
quote_evidence: Minutes from the Fed's September meeting released Wednesday indicate officials now see the AI infrastructure boom, more than tariffs, as a key force keeping goods prices elevated.
The Fed now expects inflation to stay above its 2% goal until 2029.
why_it_matters_hint: Central bank minutes tie AI investment to higher prices, which matters for household budgets and borrowing costs.
event_date: 7 Oct 2026 (minutes released; the meeting was in September)
